SMTO-GWT-0070 — SMTO can't safely reset this GPU

GUID: 95a83db6-1087-58f2-b56f-b36d60b4ba2b
Slug: gpu-reset-unsupported
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gpu

What happened

  • SMTO only resets a graphics card when it can confirm the reset is supported and safe on that computer. It couldn't confirm that here, so the GPU was not reset.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to check the reset status for this GPU. It shows which rule blocks the reset: SMTO only resets a single, physical GPU on Linux with no screen in use and MIG (GPU splitting) off.
  2. If the computer has more than one GPU, a screen running on this GPU, or is a virtual machine, ask the person who manages it to reset the card themselves. SMTO doesn't reset GPUs in those setups because it can't prove the reset won't affect other cards or displays.
  3. If the reset status says it couldn't see every program on the card, ask that person to check the NVIDIA driver. Without a complete list of programs using the card, SMTO can't be sure a reset is safe.

What success looks like

  • The reset status shows the reset as supported and safe now, and SMTO reports that the reset finished.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the computer with the GPU. Don't reset the card another way while programs might still be using it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • GPU reset was refused because preflight could not establish reset support (Linux, a single physical non-virtualized GPU, inactive display, MIG disabled, --gpu-reset available) plus a complete client list, or the provider rejected reset as unsupported.

What this means

  • Reset preflight could not establish complete client visibility and reset capability, or the provider rejected reset as unsupported. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Reset preflight could not establish complete client visibility and reset capability, or the provider rejected reset as unsupported.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect gpu.reset_status for incomplete client visibility, topology, display or virtualization restrictions.

How to fix it

  • Run gpu.reset_status for the UUID and check reset_supported, safe_now, complete and restrictions. SMTO only resets the sole physical GPU on a Linux host with display_active false and MIG disabled; multi-GPU peers, virtualized devices, active displays or incomplete client visibility must be handled by an operator outside SMTO.
  • Inspect gpu.reset_status. Multi-GPU peers, virtualized devices, active displays and unobservable clients require operator handling.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect gpu.reset_status. Multi-GPU peers, virtualized devices, active displays and unobservable clients require operator handling.

How to verify the fix

  • All supported reset prerequisites are established for the exact UUID before an authorized reset is attempted.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, kill GPU clients automatically or invent sensor values.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
